summary: A 220-second, eight-shot storyboard connecting numerical zeta geometry to the manuscript’s reciprocal-pole contradiction.
content:
220 seconds, including transitions and reading pauses. One AstraFilm(ThreeDScene), CE 0.19 Cairo, 1080p/60fps; only manim/numpy/math. Constant bone #F3EFE6; ink #202A35 typography and known-zero markers; teal #176B72 functions/arithmetic; coral #C76F51 frontiers/poles; gold #AD8542 critical spine/power saving. Landscape shading varies monotonically with height.

Reserve top 18% and bottom 16% for fixed overlays. Keep mathematical events between them. Use 36–44-point MathTex and captions ≥30; one main formula block and two short explanatory lines. Replace overlays; never bury labels behind surfaces. Camera tuples are (phi°,theta°,zoom), using set_camera_orientation/move_camera. Precompute geometry once.

1. 0–24s — Enter the valley.
Begin inside an illuminated zeta mesh; A FRONTIER FOR THE ZEROS appears for four seconds. Glide toward the first zero, (70,-95,1.15)→(58,-65,1.65). Sequential LaTeX: s=\sigma+it; h=\log(1+|\zeta(s)|); \zeta(\rho)=0. Captions identify analytic continuation and “Function-value visualization; not a physical manifold or proof.” Falling height teaches vanishing.

Use Euler–Maclaurin N=64 with eight corrections, a base 33×97 grid on [0,1.2]×[12,32], and a finer cached first-zero patch. Insert exact zero ordinates and frontier coordinates. Embedding: G=(8(\sigma-.6),.45(t-22),2h-1.6). The domain excludes the pole.

2. 24–46s — Primes enter the picture.
Match-cut mesh ribs to three actual Euler-factor magnitude ribs for p=2,3,5, sampled at \sigma=1.25. Orbit to (58,-105,.9). Hold:
\zeta(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}n^{-s}=\prod_p(1-p^{-s})^{-1},\qquad\Re s>1.
The ribs settle into a tilted complex-coordinate floor: explanatory staging. Replace captions with “Analytic continuation extends the function beyond this convergence region” and “The pole s=1 is not a zero.” Dissolve into the critical strip.

3. 46–76s — A fixed frontier.
Extrude 0<\sigma<1 around a gold \sigma=1/2 spine; camera (63,-45,.75). Keep markers fixed at t=14.134725141734693,21.022039638771555,25.01085758014569,30.424876125859513.
Five six-second formula beats:
(t_1,t_2,t_3,t_4)\approx(14.1347,21.0220,25.0109,30.4249), captioned “Sampled known zeros”;
\mathrm{RH}:\Re\rho=\tfrac12, captioned “Every nontrivial zero”;
\exists\theta<1:\ \zeta(s)\ne0\quad(\Re s>\theta,\ s\ne1);
\theta:\tfrac{11}{12}\longrightarrow\tfrac78;
\tfrac18\le\Re\rho\le\tfrac78.
Push to zoom 1.7 on the right curtain’s leftward 1/24 movement; pull back to reveal its mirrored 1/8 partner. Attribute the advance to the manuscript. Exclusion is strictly outside the boundaries; the closed central strip remains unresolved. Caption: “Finite window; assertion at every height.”

4. 76–108s — One zero, one winding.
Push into the first marker; unfold two complex planes tilted ±12° about their vertical axes. Orbit (55,-60,1)→(55,-105,1.15). Show:
s(\alpha)=\rho+0.1e^{i\alpha},\qquad w(\alpha)=\zeta(s(\alpha)).
After a five-second reveal, animate a thirteen-second counterclockwise circuit. Both points use identical indices and interpolation fractions across 513 paired vertices. Disclose separate magnifications. The computed image winds once: “This sampled zero is simple.”
For seven seconds replace with \zeta(s)\approx\zeta'(\rho)(s-\rho), labeled local approximation. For the final seven, reveal a cached reciprocal spike:
q(s)=\log(1+\min\{80,|\zeta(s)|^{-1}\}).
Captions: “Reciprocal magnitude capped at 80”; “An L-zero forces a pole of 1/L.” Reframe the peak. Local winding supplies intuition, not the manuscript’s proof.

5. 108–134s — Arithmetic supplies two views.
Match-cut to an Eisenstein lattice; travel between lifted beads, (70,-55,1.3)→(50,-85,.85).
\mathcal O_F=\mathbb Z[\tau],\quad\tau=\frac{-1+i\sqrt3}{2},\quad F=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3}).
Use vertices (m-n/2,\sqrt3n/2,.08(m^2-mn+n^2)); caption the norm lift. Define characters as multiplicative arithmetic weights; Hecke characters weight ideals.
The lattice opens into two sculpted sheets representing one completed cubic-theta sum. Reflection supplies a direct bound. Poisson fans into the principal reciprocal-L ribbon and remaining character rows. Label “Proof schematic”; shapes encode no numerical proof data. Caption: “The Hecke family is needed even for zeta.” Follow the principal ribbon.

6. 134–156s — The sharper comparison.
Orbit (50,-85,.85)→(50,-65,1.05). Replace the sum sculpture: “Part II changes the normalization.” Prime compensation adjusts junctions; unequal scales separate sheet spans. Sequential captions identify inverse second-moment and plain-polynomial fourth-moment control.
For eight seconds hold:
C(s)=s-\tfrac{11}{16},\qquad C(\tfrac78)=\tfrac3{16}.
Define J_\eta as normalized arithmetic sum, f_\eta as reciprocal-L Mellin signal; \eta is the target character and Z>0 the scale.

7. 156–202s — The contradiction.
Maintain “Conditional proof schematic.” Orbit (62,-58,.9)→(53,-82,1.05).
156–162: \beta_*>\sigma_0=\tfrac78. Define \beta_* as the supremum of 1/2 and primitive Hecke-family zero real parts in [1/2,1], excluding poles. Draw a dashed supremum curtain: it need not be attained.
162–167: |f_\eta|\le|J_\eta|+|J_\eta-f_\eta|. Two exponent ledges teach “small sum + small difference ⇒ small signal.”
167–175: hold one exact source block:
\begin{aligned}|J_\eta(Z)|&\ll_\eta Z^{C(\sigma_0)+\omega}\\|J_\eta(Z)-f_\eta(Z)|&\ll_\eta Z^{C(\beta_*)-\sigma}.\end{aligned}
Explain 0<\omega<\beta_*-\sigma_0; \sigma>0 is a saving exponent. Exponents are common across targets; constants may depend on \eta.
175–182: show \epsilon_*=\min(\beta_*-\sigma_0-\omega,\sigma)>0 and |f_\eta(Z)|\ll_\eta Z^{C(\beta_*)-\epsilon_*} in one block. Gold marks the smaller saving.
182–190: \Re s>\beta_*-\epsilon_*>\sigma_0. A translucent region extends left of the supremum. Captions connect power saving at infinity and rapid decay at zero to a holomorphic—complex analytic—Mellin transform.
190–196: Fourier inversion, identity, and |H_\eta|\ge1/2 identify the holomorphic reciprocal; deleted Euler factors are nonzero here.
196–202: the supremum supplies a hollow hypothetical zero inside the extension. Raise its reciprocal pole. Hold “A pole contradicts holomorphic continuation.” Cut away without erasing the pole by cancellation. Genuine markers remain untouched.

8. 202–220s — Summary tableau.
Return to the cached landscape, (58,-65,.75)→(50,-80,.8). Retain both curtains, unresolved central strip, gold spine and fixed markers.
202–210: \Re s>\tfrac78:\quad L(s)\ne0. Header: “Manuscript assertion.” Captions specify zeta, every Dirichlet L, and finite-order Hecke L over F; uniform in character, conductor and height; principal pole s=1 allowed.
210–214: “Full RH remains open.”
214–220: hold the sculpture beneath “OpenAI manuscript / 30 September 2026 / family 003” and “Explains the manuscript; full proof and Lean build not independently checked.”
checks: Read retained manuscript theorem, Proposition 2.1, Part II normalization, conclusion, and formalization scope.

Fresh Euler–Maclaurin checks: four zero residuals ≤1.21e-14; 3,201-point grid comparison against N=96/ten corrections differed ≤9.66e-14; computed loop winding 0.9999999999999999. Numerical evidence, not proof.
